group_assessment.waived: The two publication counts cannot be measured; the PubMed connector is unauthorized in this session, and an estimate in an integer slot is indistinguishable from a measurement. What the Methods establish is recorded here so the waiver loses nothing. research_type is experimental_lab: a mouse-genetics study from National Cheng Kung University generating TWO independent Wwox knockout strains, with behaviour (rotarod, footprint, tail suspension), transcranial motor evoked potentials, electron microscopy with immunogold, LFB/cresyl violet/TUNEL/immunohistochemistry, BrdU birthdating, western blotting and two convulsant seizure models. is_primary_group_for_disease is false for the disease and arguably true for the gene: this is a WWOX laboratory whose output is mechanism, not clinical description. Weighting: the observations are strong and internally controlled — the two-strain design exists specifically to exclude an aberrant product of the retained exon 1, and both strains agree on every behavioural measure. The pharmacology is the weak layer and is where this reading disagrees with the paper's own interpretation; see locators 1 to 4. Group standing does not repair a non-selective drug. NOTE: the waiver is per-section but the impediment is per-field.

entries.proposition: READ FROM THE IMAGE, NOT THE TEXT: lithium suppressed PTZ-induced seizures in ALL THREE genotypes, including wild-type — so the experiment does not establish a Wwox-specific rescue.
entries.snippet: d Pretreatment of a GSK3β inhibitor LiCl (60 mg/kg) suppressed PTZ-induced seizure activity in Wwox−/− mice.
entries.anchor: Figure 7d, image inspected — three stacked panels (+/+, +/−, −/−), each plotting PTZ versus PTZ+LiCl and each carrying its own significance marker. The caption and the Results text name only the −/− panel; the figure shows the same suppression in the two control genotypes.

entries.proposition: READ FROM THE IMAGE: ethosuximide, by contrast, IS genotype-specific — non-significant in +/+ and +/−, significant only in −/−. The drug the paper favours lacks the specificity the comparator has.
entries.snippet: Pretreatment of an antiepileptic drug ethosuximide suppressed PTZ-induced seizure in Wwox−/− mice (Fig. 7b), although ethosuximide pretreatment had no effects on the behavior changes in Wwox+/+ and Wwox+/− mice treated with a low dose of PTZ.
entries.anchor: Figure 7b, image inspected — PTZ versus PTZ+ETS marked n.s. in the +/+ and +/− panels and significant in the −/− panel; the text states this for ethosuximide and does not state the converse for lithium

entries.proposition: READ FROM THE IMAGE: total GSK3-beta protein is essentially unchanged across genotypes and regions; what falls is the inhibitory Ser9 phosphorylation. GSK3-beta is dis-inhibited, not more abundant.
entries.snippet: Increased activation of GSK3β was determined in the cerebellum, hippocampus and cerebral cortex of Wwox−/− mice at postnatal day 20, as evidenced by dephosphorylation of GSK3β at Ser9.
entries.anchor: Figure 7c, image inspected at the native 1946×1627 pixels and re-read at 3× on the densitometry row — pGSK3β(Ser9) cerebellum 2.7 / 3.1 / 1.3, hippocampus 3.6 / 3.5 / 2.0, cortex 3.9 / 3.8 / 2.5 across +/+, +/−, −/−; total GSK3β 2.2 / 2.4 / 2.4, 2.3 / 2.4 / 2.6 and 2.2 / 2.4 / 2.6, flat in every genotype and region

entries.proposition: The causal attribution to GSK3-beta rests on lithium, and the paper's own Discussion names lithium's other documented actions in this very system.
entries.snippet: Administration of lithium in mice has been demonstrated to attenuate PTZ-induced clonic seizure [10], and rescue Wnt-dependent cerebellar midline fusion and neurogenesis deficits early in development [38]. Lithium treatment has also been shown to induce β-catenin-mediated myelin gene expression in mouse Schwann cells and enhance remyelination of the injured peripheral nerves in mice [47].
entries.anchor: Discussion, final substantive paragraph

entries.proposition: GSK3-beta is dis-inhibited in all three brain regions of Wwox-null mice, measured by Ser9 dephosphorylation.
entries.snippet: we determined dephosphorylation of GSK3β at Ser9 (active GSK3β) in Wwox−/− mouse cerebellum, hippocampus and brain cortex by western blotting
entries.anchor: Results, 'GSK-3β inhibition ameliorates the hypersusceptibility to epileptic seizure due to Wwox loss in mice', final paragraph

entries.snippet: Injection of a potent GSK3β inhibitor lithium chloride significantly suppressed PTZ-induced epileptic seizure in Wwox−/− mice (Fig. 7d).
entries.proposition: The paper's own statement of the lithium result, restricted to the null genotype.
entries.anchor: Results, GSK-3β section, final paragraph

entries.proposition: Seizure hypersusceptibility sits on top of a structurally malformed brain — the amplifier-not-driver reading.
entries.snippet: Wwox−/− mice exhibit cerebral malformations consisting of middle interhemispheric fusion, cortical heterotopia and neuronal disorganization in the hippocampal CA1 region and display increased susceptibilities to convulsant-induced seizures. The aberrant positioning of neurons in Wwox−/− neocortex and hippocampus may cause reorganization of neuronal networks and alteration of cellular physiology that create hyperexcitable tissue.
entries.anchor: Discussion, penultimate paragraph

entries.proposition: Spontaneous seizures appear after postnatal day 12 and are triggered by ordinary sensory stressors, not only by convulsants.
entries.snippet: In our generated Wwox−/− mice, spontaneous epileptic seizures were commonly observed after postnatal day 12. Seizures were frequently induced by mild stressors including noise, strobe lights and novel cage during routine handling
entries.anchor: Results, GSK-3β section, opening

entries.proposition: Two independently targeted knockout strains were built specifically to exclude an aberrant product of the retained exon 1, and both give the same phenotype.
entries.snippet: To test if the possibly generated aberrant protein may cause phenotypes due to the presence of exon 1 in the mouse genome, we generated both exon 1- and exon 2/3/4-targeting knockout mouse strains for comparison
entries.anchor: Methods, 'Wwox gene knockout mice, rotarod performance and footprint analysis'

entries.proposition: READ FROM THE IMAGE: heterozygotes have a Tc-MEP latency statistically indistinguishable from homozygous nulls while their amplitude is normal — a dissociation, and a candidate carrier readout.
entries.snippet: an increase in Tc-MEP latency was determined in Wwox+/− mice (2.13 ± 0.22 msec; p < 0.05) when compared with the wild-type mice (Fig. 2b, c), suggesting that Wwox haploinsufficiency may cause a partial Tc-MEP deteriorative change in mice.
entries.anchor: Figure 2b–c, images inspected — amplitude +/+ versus +/− marked n.s. and +/− versus −/− significant; latency +/+ versus +/− significant and +/− versus −/− marked n.s. The text gives the +/+ comparison and not the +/− versus −/− one.

entries.proposition: Peripheral nerve involvement with Schwann cell apoptosis and onion-bulb degeneration — a PNS phenotype in a disorder usually framed as central.
entries.snippet: abnormal-shaped nerve fibers (red stars), axon demyelination (blue arrow) and onion bulb degeneration (red arrowheads) were observed in all Wwox−/− sciatic nerves examined in this study
entries.anchor: Figure 3b caption, image inspected — 5000x and 10000x electron micrographs; panel c shows immunogold cleaved caspase-3 within the Schwann cell

entries.proposition: Central hypomyelination spans commissural, association and projection fibres and the optic tract.
entries.snippet: Wwox−/− mouse brain sections showed significantly reduced myelin staining intensity in the commissural fibers (corpus callosum, and anterior and dorsal hippocampal commissures), the association fibers (cingulum), and the projection fibers emanating from corpus callosum toward striatum
entries.anchor: Results, nerve degeneration section, final paragraph; Figure 4, image inspected — rostral and caudal forebrain plus cerebellum, optic tract marked in c3/d3

entries.proposition: Cerebellar vermian lobules VI and VII are fused with Purkinje cell loss, phenocopying a Joubert-syndrome-associated lesion.
entries.snippet: Midline sagittal cresyl violet-stained section revealed foliation defects in lobules V, VI and VII of Wwox−/− cerebellum
entries.anchor: Results, cerebellar hypoplasia section; Figure 5b and 5d, images inspected — Purkinje cell counts approximately 18 versus 7 per area

entries.proposition: Neuronal maturation is delayed rather than merely reduced: the early marker DCX stays high when it should have declined.
entries.snippet: Compared with the DCX protein levels in Wwox+/+ and Wwox+/− mice, our results showed that DCX was still highly expressed in Wwox−/− brain tissues at postnatal day 14

entries.proposition: Brain malformation in this model extends to the holoprosencephaly range, i.e. a forebrain-patterning defect, not only a migration defect.
entries.snippet: Gross morphological abnormalities could be observed in Wwox−/− mouse brains from live births, ranging from microcephaly to holoprosencephaly, in which the forebrain did not properly divide into two hemispheres during embryonic development.
entries.anchor: Results, 'Wwox is required for proper neuronal migration and development', opening

entries.proposition: A structural lead on the SDR domain: WWOX may bind 17-beta-estradiol through an NSYK motif, with a proposed neuroprotective role.
entries.snippet: WWOX may interact with steroid hormone 17β-estradiol via its NSYK (Asn-Ser-Tyr-Lys) motif in the C-terminal short-chain alcohol dehydrogenase/reductase domain for neuroprotection

verbatim_locators.note:
Twenty-two locators. Eight are anchored to inspected images — four in the main figures and four in the supplementary — and they carry content the running text does not, in one case content that qualifies the paper's own conclusion. All seven main figures and all nine supplementary figures were inspected; the supplementary PDF was retrieved from the publisher's static-content endpoint after the PMC route returned HTTP 200 serving HTML. The seizure video (Additional file 2) was not retrieved.

🔴 AUDITED AND CORRECTED 2026-08-10. Every snippet was matched, character for character, against the local XML (sha256 792b5b29…, PMC6990504). SIXTEEN of twenty-two matched; FIVE did not, and all five failed for one reason: they were TRANSCRIBED AS THE PAGE READS, NOT EXTRACTED AS THE ARTIFACT CONTAINS. The markup artefacts had been silently normalised away — `Wwox <sup>−/−</sup>` extracts as `Wwox −/−` and was written `Wwox−/−`; `<xref>7</xref> b` extracts as `Fig. 7 b` and was written `Fig. b`; the reference markers `[ 10 ] [ 38 ] [ 47 ]`, the citation `(Luszczki et al., 2005)` and the cross-reference `(Fig. 2 b, c)` were dropped entirely. None of that changes meaning, but two of them LOSE INFORMATION and they are the two that matter: WHICH FIGURE a result points at, and WHICH REFERENCES support which clause — the latter being precisely the point of the locator on lithium's non-selective pharmacology. Entries 1, 3, 5, 9 and 17 are now the same span of the same sentence taken from the extracted text, each verified to match in STRICT mode, comparators intact. This is a class and not an incident: a locator captured by transcription is not a locator captured from the artifact, and the difference is invisible until a validator matches exactly. Expect it in the remaining legacy manifests. STILL OUTSTANDING, declared not fixed: entries 18 and 21 quote supplementary figure captions, which live in PMID32000863_Cheng2020_supplementary.pdf and not in the XML body — they are correct and unverifiable against the declared surface until this manifest reaches schema v2. That upgrade is blocked on something this repository cannot manufacture: the FOUR MAIN FIGURES WERE INSPECTED AT READING TIME AND NEVER PERSISTED, so eight image locators have no local artifact to name. It is the `files/` rule from the other side — the manifest survived, the evidence did not travel with it.

🔴 SCHEMA v2 UPGRADE 2026-08-10, AND A NUMBER NOTHING WAS CHECKING. The two snippets the corpus audit could not find were SUPPLEMENTARY FIGURE CAPTIONS. They are absent from the main XML because they live in the supplementary PDF, and no manifest declared that artifact — so the quotes were unverifiable by anyone, not wrong. The supplement is now declared and fingerprinted, and those two locators say what the supplementary panels show rather than repeating their captions.

🔴 RE-INSPECTING THE FIGURES TO WRITE THEM PROPERLY FOUND A TRANSCRIPTION ERROR IN AN ANCHOR. Entry 2 recorded the Figure 7c densitometry as `2.7 / 2.5 / 1.3` in cerebellum and `3.6 / 3.2 / 2.0` in hippocampus. The figure prints `2.7 / 3.1 / 1.3` and `3.6 / 3.5 / 2.0`, confirmed at 3× magnification of the native 1946×1627 image. BOTH ERRORS ARE IN THE +/− COLUMN AND BOTH PUSH THE HETEROZYGOTE DOWN: recorded, the het reads BELOW wild-type and looks intermediate; printed, it sits at or above wild-type in every region. The error manufactured a gene-dosage gradient the panel does not show — inside the manifest whose entry 18 concludes the heterozygote is indistinguishable from wild-type on every quantified developmental measure. The anchor contradicted its own manifest's conclusion for a day and nothing noticed, BECAUSE ANCHORS ARE PROSE AND NO VALIDATOR HAS EVER READ ONE. The anchor is corrected here and the verified numbers now also sit in a locator snippet, where the schema can see them.

Four artifacts declared: the JATS XML, the supplementary PDF, and the Figure 2 and Figure 7 images. Three figure locators were added for what the images carry and the text does not — Figure 7d, Figure 7c and Figure 2b-c — each verified in this run. REMAINING DEBT, NAMED: entries 10 to 13, 19 and 20 have anchors that say `image inspected` for Figures 3, 4, 5, 6 and Supplementary Figures 5c and 6b. Their snippets are body text and verify against the XML, so they are sound as text locators, but their image observations still live in prose. Those images are in the corpus; converting them is the next run on this paper, not a claim made here.

Panel/text relation is declared on all twenty-five locators. Entry 0 is deliberately `text_only`: its caption says lithium suppressed seizures in Wwox−/− mice, which is TRUE, and the panel shows the same suppression in +/+ and +/−. Incomplete is not false, so this is a QUALIFICATION, and the vocabulary has neither a value for it nor a way to point at what is qualified. That is the third instance today on the third paper. 2026-10-21 (R2 batch, scientist-b, QUESTION_DRIVEN, receipt FTR-20261021-32000863-03): six entries appended (indices 25 to 30) for the new question 'is the ethosuximide contrast time-resolved and floor-limited?'; no earlier entry was changed or contradicted; two derived crops of the declared Figure 7 PNG were added to source_artifacts.
